en: The Sūtra of the King of Dhāraṇīs of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heavens, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, the Subject Shi Hu, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven palace,
together with countless thousands of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, such as Sunirmita and others.
These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have all attained the full realization of all dharmas and turn the irreversible wheel;
in one more birth, they shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, there were also immeasurable hosts of devas along with their retinues who gathered together.
Then, the World-Honored One, seated upon a great jewel throne amidst the great assembly, looked over the gathering and desired to preach the sublime Dharma.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Subhasthita rose from his seat,
approached the World-Honored One,
prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and addressed him, saying:
World-Honored One, there are those sons of good family who,
having attained these mantra-words of the *cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī*, single-mindedly uphold them for the World-Honored Ones of the past, present, and future.
As for those who have neither seen, nor heard, nor encountered [this],
how could such a thing possibly have a cause?
We only pray that the Tathāgata will explain this to us one by one in detail.
"May all sentient beings of the future be free from doubt.
Having spoken these words, he remained gazing expectantly.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Wondrous Abiding, saying:
"You possess great skillful means to inquire about this matter.
Listen attentively, and I shall explain it for you.
The Buddha said, "O Subhūti, that son of good family dwells in the sublime."
For one who upholds these dhāraṇī verses of the wish-fulfilling jewel,
although they perform acts of benefit and dwell constantly in meritorious deeds throughout the past, the present, and the future, [the merit shall be inexhaustible].
Furthermore, because doubt regarding these dhāraṇī verses has not yet been severed, although this person dwells in the sublime and maintains them, they do not truly maintain them. Why is this?
Because this person abides in a conditioned mind.
Because they lack skillful wisdom and expedient means,
if those sons of good family have no doubt or hesitation regarding these dhāraṇī verses and focus their minds with certainty, [they shall attain success].
This is what is called being a true upholder;
this is what is called knowing the names of the Dharma-preachers of the past, future, and present;
and this is what is called seeing the characteristics of the Dharma-preachers of the past, future, and present.
They shall likewise behold the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present. Why is this?
Because such a person dwells excellently and possesses a profound understanding of the gateway of dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, because one does not abide in either faith or lack of faith;
furthermore, because one thoroughly understands that there is neither going nor coming,
neither arising nor ceasing.
Neither empty nor not empty;
neither possessing auspicious signs nor lacking auspicious signs;
neither having aspirations nor lacking aspirations.
Furthermore, because they likewise have no grasping or attachment to such dharmas,
that son of good family abides wondrously;
he is able to thus accumulate practices while abiding in non-abiding.
This is called abiding; this is the attainment of nirvāṇa.
This is called receiving, upholding, and making offerings to these dharanī verses of the wish-fulfilling jewel.
This is called attaining the meaning of being without destination and indestructible.
This is called attaining the power of being free from doubt;
this is called attaining the purity of ethical discipline (śīla);
this is called attaining the vision of the ultimate Buddhahood of all phenomena as equal, and seeing the Dharma that has been taught.
There is no self and no other; it is neither a combination nor a non-combination.
Son of good family, if you constantly cultivate this practice while abiding wondrously therein, you will attain freedom from self-defilement.
If one attains freedom from defilement, one also attains freedom from bondage.
If one is oneself free from bondage, one causes others to be free from bondage.
If both oneself and others are free from bondage, one does not abide even in liberation.
If one dwells wondrously in that which is unstained, unbound, and non-abiding liberation,
this is called attaining the dhāraṇī of the wish-fulfilling jewel.
Furthermore, within the lineage of the Tathāgatas, it is known as the supreme illumination of the Buddhas of the past.
It is also called the supreme illumination that knows the Buddhas of the future;
it is also called the supreme illumination that perceives the Buddhas of the present.
One wondrously abides in these dhāraṇī verses of the wish-fulfilling jewel.
She is indeed the mother of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
For what reason? It is because she abides for the sake of bringing benefit to those of the past, future, and present.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this sublime manner...
One who upholds these dhāraṇī verses of the wish-fulfilling jewel should know that they are said to have made offerings to and praised countless Buddhas,
and likewise are said to have heard the unsurpassed Dharma from countless Buddhas.
Furthermore, they will receive the praise and protective mindfulness of countless Buddhas,
and because they will give rise to the immeasurable merit and wisdom of the Buddhas,
those who dwell in excellence and uphold these mantra-words of the *Cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī* [shall attain these benefits].
Whatever one seeks, there is nothing that will not be obtained.
Seeking wisdom, one obtains wisdom;
seeking dhāraṇī, one obtains dhāraṇī.
If a son of good family, abiding in this sublime dwelling, should encounter someone seeking the seven treasures,
he must [provide them] within half a month.
With a pure and sincere mind, taking milk as food,
one shall make a great offering to my Buddha-clan while reciting these mantra-words of the wish-fulfilling jewel dhāraṇī.
With single-minded concentration and without interruption,
whatever one seeks shall be obtained without exception.
If anyone who dwells in this sublime state should uphold these words and phrases of the dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain their aims].
By the power and majesty of these dhāraṇī verses,
even if there were as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River,
and all the devas, nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, and even humans and non-humans therein—
Such a multitude cannot be disturbed or troubled by those with extremely evil minds;
even the constellations, including Revatī and Aśvinī, cannot harm them.
Why is this? It is because they are protected by the empowerment of the Dharma, and because they are guarded by the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, the Bodhisattva Mahāvajrapāṇi, and others;
thus, these bodhisattvas [reside] here among the gods of the Heaven of Contentment (Tuṣita).
They shall constantly provide protection even up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven,
let alone for those who recite [this] among human beings.
This "Sublime Abiding" (Miojū) is not limited to these bodhisattvas alone.
The hearts of all Buddhas also constantly protect and mindfully remember him.
Why is this? It is because he upholds these dharani verses of the wish-fulfilling jewel.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this Dharma, [remained silent].
The Bodhisattva Subhavyūha, together with the countless thousands of bodhisattvas in the assembly,
as well as the host of devas and their retinues,
having heard the Dharma, rejoiced and leaped for joy; they prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the King of Dhāraṇīs of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.
